source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And on the first{H7223} day{H3117} of the week{H7620}, at early dawn{H7925}, Miryam{H4813} Magdalena and the other{H312} Miryam{H4813} came{H935} to see{H7200} the tomb{H6913}.

one_way_hebrew: ביום הראשון מהשבוע — plain Hebrew calendar language (שבוע, the week of Gen 29:27; Lev 23:15). Greek μίαν σαββάτων ('one of the sabbaths') is itself a Hebraism — a Greek phrase that only makes sense as a rendering of Hebrew idiom; this text simply has the idiom.
בהשכמה — 'at the rising-early' (שכם, the verb of Abraham's dawn obediences, Gen 22:3): the women go to the tomb with the vocabulary of covenant earliness.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק קי״ד (Perek 114) begins here.

verses.translation: And the earth{H776} quaked{H7493}, for the messenger{H4397} of YHWH{H3068} descended{H3381} from the heavens{H8064} to the tomb{H6913}, and overturned{H2015} the stone{H68} and stood{H5975}.

one_way_hebrew: מלאך ה״ — 'the messenger of YHWH': the Tanakh's own figure, מלאך יהוה (Gen 16:7; Exod 3:2; Judg 13), where Greek has ἄγγελος κυρίου — itself a translation of this very phrase. The Hebrew text has the original construct.

והפך — 'OVERTURNED' the stone (הפך, the verb of divine overthrow — Gen 19:25; Jonah 3:4); Greek ἀπεκύλισεν ('rolled away') is gentler. And ועמד — the messenger STOOD, in the chapter whose resurrection-verb is עמד (vv. 6, 7, 8; 27:63-64): even the messenger's posture preaches standing.
greek_deviations: ועמד — 'and STOOD': Greek Matthew has the angel SITTING on the stone (ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ). Ms A adds a word after ועמד (apparatus: ועמד] + עליך A), assimilating toward the Greek's 'upon it'; the base text has the messenger standing.
textual_notes: ה״ — the ms writes ה״ ('The Name'), the scribal circumlocution for the Tetragrammaton; first occurrence in this chapter. Rendered YHWH. Howard's apparatus (28:2): ה״] השם B ('The Name' written in full), האל EF — the ms family itself glosses the circumlocution.
Howard's apparatus (28:2): ועמד] + עליך A; מן השמים] מהשמים AEF.

verses.translation: And his appearance{H4758} was like the sun{H8121}, and his garments{H899} like snow{H7950}.

greek_deviations: כשמש — 'like the SUN': Greek Matthew has 'his countenance was like LIGHTNING (ἀστραπή).' The Hebrew simile is Judg 5:31 — 'let them that love him be as the SUN when he goeth forth in his might' — and Ps 19's tent for the sun; the snow-garments are Dan 7:9's (לבושה כתלג חור, 'his garment was white as snow'). Sun and snow set the messenger in the Ancient-of-Days scene, not the storm.

verses.translation: And from fear{H6343} of him the guards{H8104} were terrified{H926} and stood{H5975} as the dead{H4191}.

one_way_hebrew: נבהלו — the terror-verb of Ps 48:6 and Job 4:5; ומפחדו — 'from the fear of HIM,' the construct פחד + suffix of Isa 2's פחד יהוה.
translation_notes: ועמדו המתים — so the base text, with the article: read most literally, 'and the DEAD STOOD' — the narrator's grim double-take in the chapter where עמד is the resurrection-verb (the guards at the tomb of the standing one become the standing dead). Mss AE read כמתים ('LIKE dead men'), matching the Greek ὡς νεκροί, and Howard's English follows them: 'stood like dead men.' Both readings are given; the base consonants carry the irony.
textual_notes: The circulating transcription reads ופחדו; the scan of Howard's text reads ומפחדו ('and from fear of him'), corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (28:4): המתים] כמתים AE.

verses.translation: And the messenger{H4397} answered{H6030} and said{H559} to the women{H802}: Do not fear{H6342}, for I know{H3045} that you are seeking{H1245} Yeshua{H3442} who was hanged{H8518}.

one_way_hebrew: אשר נתלה — 'who was HANGED': the messenger of YHWH himself names the cross with Deut 21:22's verb (תלה), as the whole Passion has (27:22-23, 38, 44). Greek τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ('the crucified one') is the Roman word; the angel of this gospel speaks Torah.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:5): לנשים] לאותו הנשים G.

verses.translation: He is not here{H369}, for already{H3528} he lives{H2416}, as he said{H559}. Therefore{H3651} come{H935} and see{H7200} the place{H4725} where the Adon{H113} arose{H5975}.

greek_deviations: שכבר חי — 'for ALREADY HE LIVES': the Hebrew resurrection is stated as life resumed (חיה — 1 Kgs 17:22; Ezek 37:5; the promise the priests quoted at 27:63, ויחיה), where Greek has ἠγέρθη, 'he was raised.' Living is a state; being raised is an event done to one — the Hebrew announces the state.

המקום אשר עמד שם האדון — 'the place where the Adon STOOD/AROSE' — Greek Matthew reads 'the place where the Lord LAY (ἔκειτο).' The Greek points at the grave-slot; the Hebrew points at the spot of the standing — עמד, Dan 12:13's resurrection-verb, the chapter's refrain.
translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads שמ with a non-final mem; the scan reads שם, corrected here.
כבר (H3528) — 'already,' Ecclesiastes' own word (Eccl 1:10): late-biblical Hebrew register.

verses.translation: And go{H1980} immediately and tell{H559} his disciples{H8527} that the Adon{H113} has already{H3528} arisen{H5975} there{H8033}; and he will be before you{H6440}, and there you will see him{H7200}, as he said{H559} to you.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew has no 'into Galilee' in the messenger's charge — 'he will be BEFORE you, and THERE you will see him'; Greek Matthew reads 'he goeth before you INTO GALILEE.' In this text Galilee enters only at v. 10, from Yeshua's own mouth.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק קט״ו (Perek 115) begins at the next verse.
Howard's apparatus (28:7): אמר] דבר A; ושם... לכם] כאשר אמר אשר תראוהו G.

verses.translation: And the women{H802} went out{H3318} from the tomb{H6913} in fear{H6343} because of seeing{H7200} the messenger{H4397}, and with great{H7227} joy{H8057} because the Adon{H113} arose{H5975} alive{H2416}; and they ran{H7323} to tell{H559} his disciples{H8527}.

one_way_hebrew: עמד חי — 'he arose ALIVE,' the two resurrection-words of the chapter joined (עמד + חי); the phrase is the Hebrew creed of the empty tomb in two syllables each.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:8): רבה] גדולה G.

verses.translation: And as they were going{H1980}, Yeshua{H3442} passed{H5674} before them{H6440}, saying{H559}: YHWH{H3068} save you{H3467}. And they drew near{H7126} to him and bowed{H6915} to him and worshiped{H7812} him.

one_way_hebrew: השם יושיעכן — 'May THE NAME SAVE YOU (fem. pl.)': the risen one's greeting is a blessing built on the root ישע — that is, on HIS OWN NAME (ישו״ע, 'YHWH saves'; cf. 1:21). In Hebrew the first word of the risen Messiah speaks his name as a benediction over the women; Greek Matthew has bare χαίρετε ('rejoice/hail'), and the wordplay — the whole theology of the greeting — vanishes. This is the kind of line no translator produces by accident: it exists because the text thinks in Hebrew.

ויקדו... וישתחוו — 'they BOWED and WORSHIPED': the Torah's fixed pair (ויקד... וישתחו, Gen 24:26, 48; Exod 4:31; 34:8 — the response to YHWH's acts of covenant faithfulness). The women answer the Name-blessing with the Tanakh's own liturgical verbs.
translation_notes: השם — here the ms writes the circumlocution in full, השם ('The Name'), where elsewhere it abbreviates ה״; rendered YHWH. The greeting is a fixed Hebrew form (the same greeting stands at Vat. Ebr. 100's 26:49 and 27:29).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:9): לפניהם] לפניהן A; השם] האל EF, ה׳ G.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: Do not fear{H6342}; tell{H559} my brothers{H251} that they go{H1980} to Galil{H1551}, and there{H8033} they will see me{H7200}.

one_way_hebrew: לאחי — 'MY BROTHERS': after the denial and flight, the risen one's word for the disciples is אחים — Joseph's word to the brothers who sold him (Gen 45:4, אני יוסף אחיכם), and Ps 22:23's vow kept: אספרה שמך לאחי, 'I will declare thy name unto MY BRETHREN' — the very psalm of 27:46, now past its forsakenness into its praise-half.

verses.translation: And while they were going{H1980}, some of the guards{H8104} came{H935} to the city{H5892} and told{H5046} the great ones{H1419} of the priests{H3548} all{H3605} that was done{H6213}.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads והבידו; the scan of Howard's text reads והגידו ('and told'), corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:11): איזה] אחד G; באו] בא G; לגדולי הכהנים] לכהני הגדולים B; הנעשה] אשר נעשה G.

verses.translation: And they met{H3259} for counsel{H6098} with the elders{H2205} of the people{H5971}, and gave{H5414} much{H7227} money to the horsemen{H6571}.

one_way_hebrew: ויעדו לעצה — 'they met by appointment for counsel': the נועדו of Ps 48:5 and the עצה of Ps 2:2's kings-in-council against YHWH and his anointed — the last council of the book, still conspiring after the tomb has opened.
translation_notes: ממון — mamon, the rabbinic word for money (the 'mammon' of Matt 6:24); no biblical Strong's entry. לפרשים — 'to the horsemen,' the same corps as 27:27 (פרשי החצר).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:12): ויעדו] יועדו AE, ויועצו G; ויעדו... העם] ויועצו מה לעשות G.

verses.translation: And they said{H559} to them: You shall say{H559} that his disciples{H8527} came{H935} by night{H3915} and stole him{H1589} while you were sleeping{H3463}.

translation_notes: The circulating transcription reads בעידכם; the scan of Howard's text reads בעודכם ('while you were'), corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:13): תלמידיו] מתלמידיו G; לילה] הלילה F.

verses.translation: And if this comes{H935} to the ear{H241} of Pilat, we will speak{H1696} with him in such a way{H6045} that he will leave you in peace{H3240}.
words: that he will leave you in peace

one_way_hebrew: יבא לאוזן — 'come to the EAR of': the Hebrew hearing-idiom (Isa 5:9 באזני יהוה; 1 Sam 8:21); Greek ἀκουσθῇ ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος translates the sense and loses the ear.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:14): בענין] + הו׳ G.

verses.translation: And they took{H3947} the coin and said{H559} as they had been taught{H3925}; and this word{H1697} is in secret{H5475} among{H996} the Jews{H3064} until this day{H3117}.

greek_deviations: בסוד — 'this word is IN SECRET among the Jews until this day': the stolen-body story is a thing whispered in council (סוד, the closed circle of Ps 83:4; Jer 23:18). Greek Matthew says the opposite surface: 'this saying is COMMONLY REPORTED (διεφημίσθη) among the Jews until this day.' The Greek describes a public rumor; the Hebrew an inside account passed within the leadership — the narrator claiming to know what was said in the סוד.
translation_notes: מטבע — the rabbinic word for coin/coinage; no biblical Strong's entry. שלמדום — 'as they had TAUGHT them' (למד): the guards recite a lesson.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:15): שלמדום] שלמדם A, שלמדים F; וזה] ואז A; הזה] omit BG.

verses.translation: And after{H310} this, when his twelve{H8147}{H6240} disciples{H8527} went{H1980} to Galil{H1551}, he appeared{H7200} to them on the mountain{H2022}

one_way_hebrew: בהר — 'on THE MOUNTAIN': the definite mountain of meeting, as at Sinai (Exod 24:12, עלה אלי ההרה); the gospel that opened its teaching on a mountain (5:1) closes its commission on one.
greek_deviations: השנים עשר — 'his TWELVE disciples': Greek Matthew reads 'the ELEVEN' (οἱ ἕνδεκα), correcting the count for Judas. The Hebrew keeps 'the twelve' as the fixed title of the body — exactly as Paul does in the earliest resurrection creed: 'he was seen of Cephas, then of THE TWELVE' (1 Cor 15:5), and as the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew also reads. Two independent Hebrew Matthews and the pre-Pauline creed agree on 'the twelve' against Greek Matthew's arithmetic.

verses.translation: where they had prayed{H6419}; and when they saw him{H7200} they worshiped{H7812} him, but there were some of them who doubted concerning him.

greek_deviations: אשר בו התפללו — 'where they had PRAYED': the mountain is known by their prayer; Greek Matthew has 'where Jesus had APPOINTED them (ἐτάξατο).' A meeting-place of prayer versus a rendezvous by order — the Hebrew's mountain is a place of worship before the worship happens.
translation_notes: שנסתפקו — 'doubted' (הסתפק, from ספק): the rabbinic term for being in halakhic doubt (ספק); no biblical Strong's entry. The doubt of the Greek (ἐδίστασαν) is here the study-house word for an unresolved question.
The circulating transcription reads ראוהי; the scan of Howard's text reads ראוהו, corrected here.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} drew near{H7126} to them and said{H559} to them: To me was given{H5414} all{H3605} the power{H3201} in the heavens{H8064} and in the earth{H776}.

one_way_hebrew: לי נתן כל היכולת — 'to me WAS GIVEN all the power': the divine passive of Dan 7:14 — ולה יהיב שלטן, 'and there WAS GIVEN him dominion... that all peoples should serve him' — the Son of Man receiving authority from the Ancient of Days. The Hebrew keeps Daniel's grammar: the power is conferred, and the Giver is the Father. Greek ἐδόθη μοι carries the same passive; the Hebrew stands one step closer to Daniel's court-scene.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:18): קרב] קרא A; אליהם] omit H.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'YHWH gave me power in the heavens and in the earth,' naming the Giver outright.

greek_deviations: THE VERSE IS TWO WORDS: לכו אתם — 'You — go.' Greek Matthew 28:19 reads: 'Go ye therefore, and TEACH ALL NATIONS, BAPTIZING THEM IN THE NAME OF THE FATHER, AND OF THE SON, AND OF THE HOLY GHOST.' The Shem Tov Hebrew has NO 'all nations,' NO baptism, and NO threefold Name — not in the base manuscript and not in any of Howard's nine manuscripts: the apparatus records no variant on this verse at all. The trinitarian baptismal formula, the proof-text of the doctrine in Matthew, is simply absent from the entire Hebrew ms family. (Letter-checked against the scan, Howard p. 150.)

The absence has an external echo in the Greek tradition itself: Eusebius of Caesarea, quoting this verse repeatedly before the council of Nicaea, cites it as 'Go and make disciples of all nations IN MY NAME,' without the threefold formula. The Hebrew text is shorter still — but the shorter readings agree in what they lack.

The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the full commission — 'go, preach to all the peoples, and immerse them in the name of the Father and the Son and Ruach Ha-Qodesh' — following the Greek; the Shem Tov family alone preserves the short ending. Where the two Hebrew Matthews agree (the twelve, v. 16; the greeting-forms), they witness a common Hebrew tradition; where Vat. Ebr. 100 matches the Greek against Shem Tov, the Shem Tov reading is the one no one had a motive to create — no medieval Jewish copyist needed a shorter Matthew, and no Christian scribe would dare produce one.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse — the two-word reading is uniform across the Shem Tov mss.

verses.translation: And have them keep{H8104} — to uphold{H6965} — all{H3605} the words{H1697} which I have commanded{H6680} you, forever{H5769}.

one_way_hebrew: ושמרו... לקיים — the double verb is Torah-covenant language: שמר, the keeping-verb of Deut 4:2 (תשמרו... את מצות), joined to קים, the upholding-verb of late-biblical covenant renewal — Esth 9:27 (קימו וקבלו, 'they confirmed and took upon them... that they would keep'), Ruth 4:7 (לקים כל דבר), Deut 27:26's לא יקים read back through Ezra's assemblies. 'Keep, to uphold, all the words I have commanded' is how Hebrew Scripture talks about the covenant's permanence; no Greek Vorlage is required or even helpful — the Greek of 28:20 (τηρεῖν) translates שמר but has nothing behind לקיים or עד עולם.

עד עולם — the last two words of the Hebrew gospel are the Psalter's refrain of the Torah's duration: 'the word which he commanded to a thousand generations' (Ps 105:8), 'all his commandments are sure; they stand fast for ever and ever' (Ps 111:7-8), 'thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth FOR EVER (לעולם)' (Ps 119:160).
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew 28:20 reads: 'teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I AM WITH YOU ALWAY, EVEN UNTO THE END OF THE WORLD.' The Shem Tov Hebrew ends the gospel: ושמרו אותם לקיים כל הדברים אשר ציויתי אתכם עד עולם — 'and have them keep — to uphold — all the words which I have commanded you, FOREVER.' The 'I am with you' promise-clause is absent from all mss; and where the Greek's πάντα ('all things') floats free, the Hebrew's עד עולם binds the commandments themselves: the last words of the Hebrew gospel are that what he commanded is to be kept forever. The gospel that said 'not one yod or stroke shall pass from the Torah' (5:18) closes on the permanence of the commandments.

The one variant Howard records: ושמרו] ולמדו A B — mss A and B read 'and TEACH them' for 'and have them KEEP' (the transcription's footnote 189 confirms). Even the fullest variant text of the Hebrew ending contains teaching and keeping only — no nations, no baptism, no formula.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (28:20): ושמרו] ולמדו AB.
Letter-checked against the scan (Howard p. 150): the verse reads exactly ושמרו אותם לקיים כל הדברים אשר ציויתי אתכם עד עולם, and the book ends here — no further text follows in any Shem Tov ms.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 28 in the Shem Tov Hebrew ends the gospel with the most consequential short reading in the book. (1) 28:19-20 read, in their entirety: לכו אתם — 'You — go' — ושמרו אותם לקיים כל הדברים אשר ציויתי אתכם עד עולם — 'and have them keep, to uphold, all the words which I have commanded you, FOREVER.' There is NO trinitarian baptismal formula, NO 'teach all nations,' NO 'I am with you alway' — in the base manuscript or in any of Howard's nine mss; the only recorded variant is ושמרו] ולמדו AB ('and teach them,' fn 189). The commission of the Hebrew gospel is the keeping of the commandments forever — the ending Matt 5:17-19 predicts — and its last two words are עד עולם. Eusebius' pre-Nicene citations of Greek 28:19 ('make disciples of all nations IN MY NAME,' without the formula) show the Greek tradition itself once read shorter; the Shem Tov Hebrew is the shortest and most self-consistent form. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the full Greek-style commission — the two Hebrew Matthews divide exactly at the doctrinal seam. (2) The resurrection is told in Hebrew verbs of standing and living: the Adon עמד חי, 'arose alive' (28:6-8; Dan 12:13's עמד, the verb the priests quoted at 27:63-64); 'come see the place where the Adon AROSE' — where Greek has 'where the Lord LAY' (28:6); even the guards ועמדו המתים, 'stood as the dead' (28:4, base text with the article — mss AE read כמתים). (3) 28:9: the risen one's first word is the greeting השם יושיעכן — 'May THE NAME save you' — a blessing built on the root of his own name (ישו״ע); Greek χαίρετε erases it. The women answer with the Torah's pair ויקדו וישתחוו (Gen 24:26). (4) 28:16 reads 'his TWELVE disciples' where Greek counts eleven — with 1 Cor 15:5's 'the twelve' and Vat. Ebr. 100; and the mountain is 'where they had PRAYED' (28:17), not 'where Jesus appointed them.' (5) 28:2: the מלאך ה״ (messenger of YHWH — the ms writes ה״, and ms B spells השם, EF האל) descends, OVERTURNS the stone and STANDS (Greek: sits); his appearance is 'like the SUN' (28:3, Greek: lightning; Dan 7:9's snow-garments). (6) 28:15: the stolen-body story is kept בסוד — 'in secret' among the leadership 'until this day' — where Greek says it was 'commonly reported': the Hebrew claims inside knowledge of the council (28:12 = Ps 2:2's עצה). (7) 28:18 keeps Dan 7:14's divine passive — 'to me WAS GIVEN all the power in the heavens and in the earth' (Vat. Ebr. 100: 'YHWH gave me'). The angel names the cross with Torah's verb — 'Yeshua who was HANGED' (28:5, נתלה). Shem Tov's section headings fall at vv. 1 (Perek 114) and 8 (115); the gospel ends at 28:20 with no further text in any ms.
